headline: Kerala HC: Section 194A(3) TDS on co-op society interest governed by earlier rulings
reference: Elampal Service Co-Operative Bank Ltd v. Union of India, WP(C) No. 3760 of 2026, Kerala High Court, 2026:KER:78379
summary_points: Issue: validity of the Section 194A(3) proviso (Finance Act, 2020) requiring TDS where a co-operative society's turnover exceeds ₹50 crore.
The petitioner, a co-operative credit society, also sought exemption from TDS on interest from other co-operative societies, and quashing of a notice from the 4th respondent.

Held: the Court noted that Vellangallur Peoples Welfare Co-op Society upheld the provision's validity, and that the Division Bench in Cheruthazham Service Co-op Bank (WA 2653/2025) clarified that co-operative banks are exempt from TDS.
The writ petition was disposed of; applicability to the petitioner is governed by the principles in those decisions.
Practical impact: no fresh ruling, but TDS under Section 194A(3) for Kerala co-operative banks and societies will follow the Vellangallur and Cheruthazham principles.
who_is_affected: Co-operative banks and credit societies, especially in Kerala, that receive interest from other co-operative societies, and the banks that deduct TDS on it.
action_required: Review TDS deduction and collection practices under Section 194A(3) against the Vellangallur and Cheruthazham rulings and read the full judgment for the petitioner-specific position.

The Kerala High Court has disposed of Elampal Service Co-Operative Bank Ltd v. Union of India (WP(C) No. 3760 of 2026) on 9 October 2026, without a fresh ruling on the merits.

The petitioner challenged the proviso to Section 194A(3) inserted by the Finance Act, 2020. It requires TDS where a co-operative society's turnover exceeds ₹50 crore. It also sought exemption from TDS on interest received from other co-operative societies, and quashing of a notice.

The Court relied on two earlier rulings. Vellangallur Peoples Welfare Co-operative Society upheld the constitutional validity of Section 194A(3). The Division Bench in Cheruthazham Service Co-operative Bank (WA 2653/2025) clarified that co-operative banks are exempt from TDS.

The petition was disposed of, and the provision's applicability to the petitioner will follow those principles.

For co-operative banks and societies, and for the entities deducting tax, the earlier decisions are the reference point for the TDS position.
